subject: Day 60: texture-book reading
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 60 lands in the easy stretch between the colic peak and the 4-month sleep regression. Avi tracks fluidly now and engages more, so it is the right week to upgrade the book rotation from pure high-contrast to narrative and tactile pages.

Action items
- Add two texture or simple-narrative board books to the rotation today, keeping one or two high-contrast favorites in the mix. Tactile pages now recruit touch alongside vision, and reading aloud is one of the highest-effect-size inputs for later expressive vocabulary. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Hold the 2-month visit's six vaccines as the baseline and confirm the 4-month visit is on the calendar, window day 112-126, when RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2 are due. AAP immunization policy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/
- Run a 2-4 hour daycare or nanny trial this week if you are returning to work soon, since standard 12-week US leave ends in roughly two to three weeks and you want the handoff tested before it counts.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Lingering low-grade fussiness up to about 72 hours after the 2-month shots, and spit-up volume tapering as the upper esophageal sphincter matures.
- [monitor] Asymmetric movement or a persistent head turn to one side suggesting torticollis; document which side and raise it at the 4-month visit.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting unrelated to vaccines, a new heart murmur, or a clear drop in wet-diaper output.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher in an infant under 90 days, blue lips, or labored breathing warrant a same-day call now, and 911 for blue lips.

Enrichment opportunities
- Graduate the rotation from purely high-contrast cards to texture board books and simple narrative, letting him pat and mouth the tactile pages so touch and vision work together. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Sing live across varied tempos, a slow lullaby into a fast clapping song and back, while his tempo discrimination is sharpening; varied input preserves perceptual range. Trainor infant music study: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Hold coo conversations in extended turns, answering each vocalization and pausing two to three seconds for his reply; vowel-consonant combinations like goo are starting, and conversational turns predict later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Keep cumulative tummy time at 60-plus minutes a day in short bouts, placing a toy just out of reach to motivate stretching and forearm push-ups. AAP tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 56-70 (now): 2-month well visit window, with HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, and IPV #1 if not yet done.
- Day 57-72 (now): post-vaccine 24-72h window for low-grade fever, drowsiness, and fussiness.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit, with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete

- Turns head toward the sound of your voice
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Localizes sound source. Worth raising with the pediatrician if absent at the 4-month visit.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/turns-head-toward-sound/complete

- Makes sounds back when you talk to him
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Conversational turn-taking. Foundation for later vocabulary growth.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/makes-sounds-back/complete

- Opens mouth when she sees the breast or bottle
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Anticipatory recognition — feeding is now associated with the sight, not just the sensation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/opens-mouth-for-breast/complete
